`Club_Records::update_league_position_records(league, all_time)`: sorts the table of each league stage and stores
each club's best and worst league position for the season and, with the second argument, all time (queueing the news
item for a human club or national side).
A null league, or one whose +0x44 is not 0xff, gives the error boxes and 0. In each league of the chain
(league_stage_chain) it sorts the table (`sort_table`) and, for each row that has games (+0x11) and a club, through the
season records (`get_season_record`) and the all-time records (`get_all_time_record`, created when missing): best position (type 1,
`exe::club_records_record_type_applies`) and worst (type 2). The position is written when there is no record yet (−1), when the competition (the id
of the first league) has a higher reputation (best) or a lower one (worst), or when it is the same competition with
a better or worse position: it stores the position (+0/+7), the competition (+1/+8) and the year (+5/+0xc; 0 for the
season, `key_nation_get_club_season_year` for all time). For all time (with `all_time`; an id above [0xae2378] also counts as "no record"),
the news queue (club_records_queue_record_news). Returns 1.

`Club_Records::send_record_news()` (SEH frame without a destructor): delivers the news item of each queued record
(human club or national side) and empties the queue.
Without a queue (+0x24), returns 1. For each record in the queue (6 bytes: club id, type, period at +5) of a human
club (`news_club_has_human_manager`) or a national side (`exe::database_is_national_team`): the news item 0x3e8 (local) is filled by `exe::club_records_write_record_news_fields` with the season
record (period 2, `get_season_record`) or the all-time record (`get_all_time_record`), without creating them; it is delivered to the nation
(`send_to_nation_managers`) of the national side or to the club's manager (`send_to_club_manager`). A queue with capacity (+0x28) of 100 or more is
freed (`exe::crt_free`) and +0x24/+0x28 are zeroed. The count (+0x2c) goes back to 0. Returns 1.

`Club_Records::pick_fans_player_of_year(club, record)`: picks the fans' player of the year from the club's squad:
the best score among the players with games above the minimum; stores his reference at record +0x371 and returns 1,
or 0.
Without games (signed +0x10 of the club's 106-byte entry in [this+0x1c]) and with reputation (+0x80) below 3000,
returns 0. With the factor 0.6, falling by 0.1 while nobody has been chosen and it is above 0.2: the minimum number
of games is +0x10 × factor (_ftol); among the 50 squad slots (+0xd7), the players (+0x61, id below [0xae2364]) of
the club (+0x39) with statistic 6 (`get_category_record` over [0xb74350]) whose games are above 0 and above the minimum (signed
16 bits), the one with the highest score (`fan_rating`: average + 0.025 × +2 + 1/60 × +6, club and player likes; it
must be above −1000). Nobody: 0; otherwise his reference (`fill_staff_name_ref`) at record +0x371 and 1.

`Club_Records::update_transfer_fee_records(transfer)`: updates the buyer's paid record and the seller's received
record, for the season and all time (fee, reference, other club, date, loan).
The person (+0xc) and the buying club (+8); the person's contract (`exe::contract_manager_get_contract` over [0xae1050], kept in [0xae1080])
gives the seller (+4). The buyer's season (`get_season_record`) and all-time (`get_all_time_record`) records are fetched (created when
missing); without a seller, returns 1. A fee (+0x1b) above the season paid record (+0x313) becomes the record: the
fee, the person's reference (`fill_staff_name_ref`), the seller, today's date and the loan flag (+4 ≠ 0); if it is above the
all-time record it is copied there, and if it passes 1000 × (reputation + 300): the record goes to the news queue
(`queue_record_news`, 0x1c, if it is not there yet) and the manager (+0xbf) comes to favour the person (`staff_add_favoured_staff`, forced). The
same for the seller in the received record (+0x33c; the queue with 0x1d, without the favouring). Returns 1.

`Club_Records::add_transfer_totals(fee, buyer, seller)`: adds the fee to the seller's season income and the buyer's
season spending, raises the all-time records and queues the record news (0x1f, 0x1e) above (+0x80 + 500) × 1000.
The seller adds `fee` to the income for the season (+0x36b of the season record `get_season_record`; −1 = nothing yet: the fee
is stored) and zeroes the year (+0x36f); above the all-time record (`get_all_time_record`, same field), the record becomes the

the same for spending (+0x365, year +0x369, news 0x1e), but the minimum is checked against the OLD record and
without the year. The records are created when missing (second argument 1). A null buyer or seller: nothing, 1.
Returns 1.

Updates the FIFA rankings on the 18th: drops the results older than a year, sorts the histories, rolls the yearly
totals and redoes scores and positions.
Ret 4: `FIFA_RANKINGS::update_rankings(date)` (from the national sides' day `national_teams_daily_update`): only on the 18th (`exe::date_get_day_of_month`).
Stores the date in +5 (`exe::date_operator_3d`) and, in each nation (`[0xae2350]` entries), removes from the history the results
older than a year (year + 1 before today's, or the same year with the month before today's, `exe::date_get_month`), putting the
last one in its place; the loop goes from the low byte of the count − 1 down to 0, as in the original. Then sorts
the history by points (qsort `exe::crt_qsort` with `compare_result_points_desc`). In the month stored in +4, with the year different from that
of `[0xdd6ec8]`, the yearly totals move one slot (+0x14 → +0x28) and +0x14 is zeroed. Finally the scores (`recalculate_scores`)
and the positions: the order (`collect_ranked_order`) gives position + 1 in +0x10, with the previous one in +0x12; the order
vector is freed (`exe::crt_free`).

Recalculates the scores: the year total from the best eight results and the score from the totals of this year and

(0x54c8e0), with fewer than nine results the total is (+0x18 + eight) / (count + 8) × 8 (with no results, +0x18).

truncated) × `[0x96a350]`.

Matches a container item name against a pattern with `*` (`*.` goes to the last dot), case-insensitively; the "{
Empty }" slot never matches.
`zipdir_match_filename_pattern(pattern, name)`: 1 if the item's name matches the pattern. "{ Empty }" (0xad6ad8, the
empty slot of the unpack list) never matches; a name equal to the pattern, or an empty pattern, matches; otherwise
letter by letter, case-insensitively (`exe::utils_char_to_lower`, only the low byte). `*.` skips the name up to the last dot; `*`
followed by anything else only matches if it is the end of the pattern. As in the original, the pattern ending
before the name also matches ("abc" matches "abcdef").
reads the container header and returns dword +4 (0x16 .sav, 0x17 .qst; 0x14 on failure)

Turns each folder file matching the pattern (FindFirstFile) into a container item: zopen for writing, fread/zwrite
in 0x30d40-byte blocks, zclose.
`zadd_matching_files(path, folder, pattern, a4, kind)`: each file in the folder that `FindFirstFile` finds with the
pattern (`exe::file_find_first`/`exe::file_find_next`, files only, in the system's order) becomes a container item: `zopen` for writing
(`exe::zopen`, creates the container with `a4`/`kind` if it does not exist) + `fread` in blocks of 0x30d40 into the
item's read buffer (+0x41705) + `zwrite` (`zipdir_zwrite`) + `zclose` (`zclose`). 1 at the end; 0 if nothing matches. A
file that does not open or an item refused: the error box (zipdir.cpp 797 / 805) and 0, without closing the search
(as the original).

Turns each container item whose name matches the pattern into a folder file (zopen for reading, zread in
0x30d40-byte blocks, fwrite).
`zextract_matching_files(path, folder, pattern)`: copies the names of the index's 1000 slots (the empty ones as "{
Empty }") into a list of 0x104 bytes per name (malloc `exe::crt_malloc`); each name that matches the pattern (`zipdir_match_filename_pattern`) and
opens (`zopen` reading, a4 0x15, kind 4) becomes a file in the folder ("wb"), in blocks of 0x30d40 read by `zread`
(`zipdir_zread`) into the item's write buffer (+0x72445). 1 if it extracted any. A file that cannot be created: 0 (closes
the item).
Stack garbage in the original: on the error paths (out of memory for the list, a container that does not open or is
of an unknown type) it closes the item from a local variable that was never written; here it starts at 0. Out of
memory for the index, the error box (zipdir.cpp 642) writes the name "zipdir" over the answer (the same stack slot)
and the list carries on without the names (memory from the allocation).

Reads from the item like fread, clipped at the item end; on type 4 decodes the RLE (a run may span calls).
`zread(buf, size, count, z)` like `fread`, inside the item opened for reading (otherwise 0): the request (`size ×
count`, int) is clipped at the end of the item and added to the logical position. Type 3: a direct `fread` of
`request / size` items. Type 4: decodes the RLE; a run can span calls (+0x10 of +0x14). Returns `request / size`
(signed division, as the original: `size` 0 crashes both).

Writes to the item like fwrite and adds to the size in the index; on type 4 encodes the RLE (runs of up to 0x7f kept
across calls).
`zwrite(buf, size, count, z)` like `fwrite`, in the item opened for writing (otherwise 0): adds `size × count` to
the item's size in the index and to the logical position. Type 3: a direct `fwrite` (returns whatever it returns).
Type 4: encodes the RLE byte by byte, keeping the run in +0x18/+0x14 between calls; a different byte closes the run
(1 with byte <= 0x80 goes out as a literal, otherwise the pair 0x80 + n, byte); at 0x7f the pair goes out and the
run restarts. Returns `count`.

Closes a container item: when writing, flushes the buffer, closes the pending RLE run and rewrites header and index
at the start; closes the file and frees the item.
`zclose(&z)`. Writing: flushes the write buffer; if the item has a size, on type 4 it closes the pending run
directly in the file (literal or pair, as in zwrite) and rewrites the whole header + index (0x416ec bytes) at the
start (`fseek` 0). Reading: clears the read cursors. Closes the FILE, frees the ZFILE and clears the pointer.
